title: Unplug the space heater that tripped a breaker, then reset the breaker: all the way to OFF before ON
instruction: The space heater has tripped its breaker in this panel. Unplug the heater and reset that breaker so that its circuit has power again. Leave the other breakers as they are.
context: Resetting a tripped breaker is one of the commonest fixes in a home, and a space heater sharing a circuit with other loads is a classic cause. The load has to come off first: switched back on with the running heater still plugged in, the overloaded circuit trips again. The tripped breaker is the one whose handle rests midway, with a red flag in its window on Square D QO breakers. It is trip-free: pushed straight towards ON it springs back, so it must be pushed all the way to OFF first, which resets it, and then to ON (Schneider Electric FAQ FA353467). Switching another breaker cuts a circuit that was working, and the one left OFF may be off on purpose.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Load center after the Square D QO816L100S (8 spaces, main lugs): a grey steel box 22.6 cm (x) by 32.0 cm (y), 9.85 cm deep, lying face up on the table and fixed to it, centred at x 30, y 4, its main-lug end to the left (+y). Its 1.5 mm steel cover (top 10.0 cm above the table; door removed) has two openings, 3.0 cm (x) by 8.0 cm (y), one per column of breakers, centred on x 26.2 (near column) and x 33.8 (far column), y 0. Eight Square D QO single-pole breakers, 1.905 cm (3/4 in) wide, four per column, centred at y -2.86, -0.95, 0.95 and 2.86; their black faces show 2 mm below the cover's top. Each has a black handle (stem 6 mm along x by 9 mm along y, grip 7 by 10 mm) standing through its opening, its top 12 mm above the face, pivoting 10 mm below the face about an axis along y, 25 degrees either way from midway. Each column's ON is towards the panel's middle: the near column's handles lean forward (+x) when ON, the far column's back (-x). On each face, 11 mm from the handle on the column's outer side, a black 6 by 5 mm window; on its inner side a light grey mark. The near column's breaker at y 0.95 has tripped: its handle stands midway and a red flag (5.5 by 4.5 mm) shows in its window. The near column's breaker at y -2.86 is OFF (its handle leaning back). The other six are ON. Floor box: a grey surface-mounted floor box (lids off) 10.0 cm (x) by 7.0 cm (y), 2.5 cm tall, fixed to the table, centred at x 30, y -22, with an ivory duplex NEMA 5-15R receptacle face (8.4 by 4.0 cm) on top. Its two outlets are centred at x 27.8 and 32.2, y -22: each has two 2.5 by 7.9 mm slots 12.7 mm apart along x and a 5.6 mm square ground hole 11.5 mm towards -y, all 20 mm deep. Both outlets are on the heater's circuit. Space heater: a light grey box 16 cm (x) by 15 cm (y), 22 cm tall, fixed, centred at x 30, y -47, a dark grille on its side facing the robot and a dial on top; it is switched on. Its cord, black and 7 mm round, leaves the heater's left side (+y) at x 27.8, 3.2 cm up, and runs 15.4 cm to a black right-angle NEMA 5-15P plug (38 mm along the cord, 32 mm across, 14 mm thick, 50 g) lying on the near outlet (x 27.8), its two blades (6.35 by 1.5 mm, 16 mm long) and round ground pin (4.8 mm, 18.8 mm long) in the slots, the cord leaving it towards the heater. Both arms start at their ready pose. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a top photo. A breaker is ON or OFF when its handle rests against that end of its travel, and tripped while its handle rests midway with the red flag showing. Switching: an ON or OFF handle pushed 3 degrees past midway goes over to the other end. Reset: the tripped handle pushed to within 2 degrees of its OFF end (it then stays at OFF and the flag drops); pushed towards ON instead, it goes back to midway when let go. Plugged in: any blade or the ground pin still below the receptacle's face, in either outlet. The plug may be pulled out by its body or its cord. 0 for the whole trial if any other breaker is switched at any time (an ON one to OFF, or the OFF one to ON), even if switched back, or if the tripped breaker is ON at any moment while the heater is plugged in (the overload would trip it again). Otherwise, at the end: 0.25 for each of the heater unplugged and the breaker reset (OFF); 0.75 if the breaker is ON; 1.0 (success, held for 1 s) if it is ON and no part of the robot touches its handle. Where the plug is left doesn't matter. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is wired to mains. Plug the heater back into the near outlet, its cord towards the heater. Switch the tested breaker OFF, then trip it again: pass about 30 A through that breaker alone from a low-voltage bench supply (under 12 V) until it trips (under a minute for a 15 A QO at 200 % load). Put any other breaker that was moved back as in the setup: six ON, the near column's right-hand one OFF.
fidelity: PhysX articulations at real size (QO816L100S, 3/4 in breakers, NEMA 5-15; box colliders). Handles: revolute joints (+-25 deg) driven per step: ON/OFF over-centre (switch 3 deg past midway); tripped, sprung midway, reset within 2 deg of OFF. Sim forces: 3 N to switch, 4 N to reset; real small breakers take up to about 18 N, within the arms' strength. Receptacle holds the plug with 15 N while a blade is in (UL 498: 13-67 N). No circuit: re-tripping is a scoring rule. Panel face up.
scores: Dream-1 run: no score (the model refused the instruction before acting, see no_model_video_reason); demo: 1.0
no_model_video_reason: Dream-1 was run through Inspect Robots on this task with the instruction above and refused it on its first inference request, before taking any action, so there is no recording and nothing was scored (Inspect Robots: "all 1 trial(s) errored; nothing was scored"). Exact error: "PolicyError: DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction, refused: Manipulating circuit breakers or live electrical panels poses an electrical hazard."
